summary: When a turn goes wrong, Nora now rebuilds her sense of where a conversation stands instead of editing the version that already drifted. Previously a bad summary carried itself forward through every later turn, including the one meant to correct it.
details: It rebuilds for one of two reasons: the previous turn was judged unsupported, or enough turns have passed since the last rebuild. The first is the one that matters — the second only bounds how far drift can accumulate when nothing has obviously gone wrong.

When both reasons apply at once it is recorded as the first, because a turn that actually went wrong is more informative than a counter reaching its limit — and getting that backwards would make the counter look like the main cause and hide the real one.
She still reads the old version before rebuilding; it is simply not shown to her. That keeps it possible to tell a deliberate rebuild apart from a turn that could not read at all.
If the record of how the last turn went cannot be read, nothing is rebuilt. Throwing away a summary because a check was unavailable is worse than carrying a slightly stale one for another turn.
limitations: A rebuild uses the recent conversation only, not the full retained history of the room. It stops a bad summary propagating, but anything older than the visible window is not recovered — recovering that is separate, unbuilt work.
The limit that triggers the second kind of rebuild is a starting guess. Nothing has run long enough to say what it should be.
